status: G4 pilot: processed, compressed and reviewed; ships as g4-mule, in Chapters VII, XI and XII (on the web in Chapter XI only)
use: A pair of draught mules, unhitched, standing beside the covered carriage (carpentum) in the camps' courts beyond the board (Chapters VII, XI and XII): one model set out twice.

generator.prompt: A Roman draught mule of the mid-3rd century AD standing square: all four legs straight and vertical, evenly spaced, head raised and facing forward, long ears upright, tail hanging straight down, symmetrical. A tall, strong mule about 1.5 metres at the withers with a light grey-dun coat, darker lower legs, a dark stripe along the spine, a pale muzzle and belly and a short upright dark mane, wearing a plain leather headstall with a short lead rope and a broad leather breast strap. No cart, no shafts, no yoke, no saddle, no packs, no rider, no people. Realistic proportions, anatomically accurate. Single isolated model with complete geometry from every side and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above. No ground plane, no display plinth, no text or inscriptions, no modern objects, no fantasy elements.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the camps in the desktop build at High
review.notes: Paler and slighter than asked: nearly white rather than grey-dun, with a slim, horse-like body. Its long upright ears, dark mane and tail, leather headstall and breast strap say mule, so it was kept: 2.07 m long and 1.95 m to its ear tips. In Chapters XI and XII the pair stand unhitched beside the covered carriage and read as a pale team; from the camp camera the long ears are less plain than in the four views.
